correctness.rationale: The coefficient extraction gives \(B\equiv-T\pmod p\). In the exceptional case \(l+1=ap\), Frobenius gives \(F^l\equiv F^{-1}\pmod{x^p}\), so \(B\) is the \(x^{p-1}\)-coefficient of \(F' /F\). Factoring \(F=\prod(1-\alpha_i x)\), that coefficient is \(-\sum\alpha_i^p=-(\sum\alpha_i)^p=1\) because the linear coefficient of \(F\) is \(1\). Thus \(T\equiv-1\pmod p\). The nonexceptional branch follows from differentiating \(F^{l+1}\). Exact-arithmetic finite tests over all primes \(p\le19\), \(l\le3p+2\), and \(m\le6\) agree. No computational test is used to justify the infinite step.
